title: Library domain model
idea: The library domain model separates the catalog title (Book) from each physical item (BookCopy), and links Members to copies through Loans and to titles through Reservations.

analogy.text: A recipe card and the dishes cooked from it. One card, many plates; each plate is eaten by one person at a time.
analogy.breaks: Plates are not returned; a BookCopy comes back and circulates again.

points: A Book is one title by ISBN; it has one or more BookCopy items.
A Loan links one BookCopy to one Member, with a due date.
A Reservation links a Member to a Book, never to a specific copy.
FinePolicy is an interface, so the fine rule can change without touching Loan.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: One Book title owns many BookCopy items. Each copy has its own barcode id.

edges.label: for 1
edges.caption: A Loan is for exactly one copy. A copy has at most one open Loan.

edges.label: by 1
edges.caption: A Member has zero to five open Loans under the v1 policy.

edges.label: waits for 1
edges.caption: A Reservation points at the title, so any returned copy can serve it.

edges.label: by 1
edges.caption: Each Reservation belongs to one Member and keeps a sequence number for queue order.

edges.label: has
edges.caption: LoanStatus is an enum. The flows page turns it into a state machine.

edges.label: is-a
edges.caption: PerDayFine is one FinePolicy: a rate per late day, capped per loan.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for data that never changes, classes for things whose status moves. Constructors refuse invalid objects.

walk.text: One Book title with two physical copies and one Member.
A Loan for copy CP-1, due 14 days after a fixed date.
The fine policy prices a 4-day late return and a very late one.
Two invalid objects are refused: a due date before the borrow date and a blank ISBN.
BookCopy is mutable only in status. Status lives on the copy, not on the Book.
The Loan constructor guards its invariant: the due date comes after the borrow date.
Early returns give zero late days; the cap limits the fine per loan.

pitfalls: Do not put an availability flag on Book; status belongs to each BookCopy.
Keep fines as long minor units; never use double for money.
Do not store the fine on Loan before return; compute it from dates.

quiz.q: What does LibraryModel print for the very late return?
quiz.why: Thirty late days at 1000 each is 30000, but `Math.min` with the cap of 10000 wins.

takeaway: A Book is the title; a BookCopy is the thing that gets borrowed.

starters: Why does a Reservation point at Book instead of BookCopy?
Should OVERDUE be stored or computed from the due date?
How would I add DVDs or magazines to this model?
